record.name: Venezuela
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The National Assembly approved an AI bill at first reading on 19 November 2024. MINCYT said on 7 May 2026 that it was in its second discussion and envisaged a national AI institute focused on human-centred AI, bias and local data infrastructure; its remit to evaluate advanced models remains unconfirmed.

A generic AI institute and broad bill objective of evaluating AI do not establish the required model capability/severe-risk remit; the complete bill remains unread. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: The recorded es queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. The earlier English-search pass on 17 October 2026 left the then-recorded national or official-language coverage unchanged; the work is described below. The additional status review recorded Spanish and English searches; no primary English translation of the institutional provisions was found. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5, 6; 7, 8; 9, 10. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English and Spanish; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: MINCYT's digital-ecosystem account and KPMG's analysis of a MINCYT ethics code establish policy context. Their retrieved passages do not establish two substantive independent institute-status evidence origins. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The ministry and National Assembly provide primary evidence about the pending AI law and proposed national AI institute. Their descriptions do not establish the required remit covering advanced models. An older unofficial draft contains deployment-related risk assessment, leaving the current mandate unresolved.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Science and Technology (MINCYT)
related_bodies.role: It leads the national AI programme as the science ministry. Its May 2026 account describes a prospective national AI institute addressing bias and local data infrastructure. The account does not establish a qualifying remit to evaluate advanced models.

related_bodies.name: Agencia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (proposed in the AI bill)
related_bodies.role: The 13 November 2024 draft reproduced on an unofficial legal website proposes a public institute under the science ministry with standards, registries, supervision and sanctions. Article 12.16 includes model-risk assessment for exceptional authorisations of otherwise unacceptable AI uses; a remit to test advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks remains unconfirmed.

record.notes: The National Assembly's own account confirms first reading on 19 November 2024. The freshly retrieved MINCYT account is dated 7 May 2026, correcting the earlier 8 May date; it describes a prospective Instituto Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial but does not define a mandate to test advanced models. A scanned draft dated 13 November 2024 was retrieved from an unofficial legal website. Articles 11–12 describe a National AI Agency as a public institute under the science ministry, with technical standards, registries, supervision and sanctions. Article 12.16 includes assessing model risks when exceptionally authorising otherwise unacceptable AI uses. That provision should not be described as having no evaluation mechanism, but it does not establish general-purpose or frontier-model capability or behaviour-risk testing. The mirror contains 29 pages numbered 6–34, and only the relevant institutional provisions were visually inspected. The current official full bill and any later adopted text were not found; the relationship between the agency in this draft and the institute named by MINCYT remains unresolved. Spanish and English searches found no later qualifying designation. The broader national plan and ethics code were not rechecked.

next_check.reason: Obtain the current official bill and determine whether MINCYT's prospective institute has a general-purpose/frontier model evaluation mandate.
